waves.name: Environment and dataset definition jobs
waves.rationale: Jobs that run only utilities (IDCAMS, RACF, FTP, listing) and touch no dataset another entry point uses. In a refactor they are replaced by target-platform provisioning, not ported line by line. They prove the pipeline and the build, and carry no business logic.
waves.unblocks: Nothing in the business flows. It does give the team a target environment, and it settles where the VSAM datasets that waves 2 to 7 read and write will live. Treat it as a chore, not a deliverable a stakeholder will name.

waves.name: Master file read and list jobs
waves.rationale: Read-only batch programs over the account, card, customer and cross-reference masters, plus CBIMPORT, which reads the export file. They have no computed calls, and each is the first consumer of a record layout that waves 5 and 6 write. They are the cheapest place to prove that the target reads a master file byte for byte the way COBOL does.
waves.unblocks: The record-layout copybooks CVACT01Y, CVACT02Y and CVCUS01Y become tested, versioned data contracts in the target. Waves 5 and 6 reuse them.

waves.name: Sign-on, menus and read-only inquiry screens
waves.rationale: Online screens that write nothing another entry point uses. COSGN00C, COMEN01C and COADM01C are one call cycle and COTRN00C and COTRN01C are another, so each cycle moves whole. COMEN01C and COSGN00C each have 12 callers, so this wave holds the menu and sign-on shell that every later online wave depends on. Six of the seven programs make computed calls, so the menu's reachable targets are not proven.
waves.unblocks: Wave 7 online writers. They need the sign-on and menu shell in place before any screen can be reached in the target. The transaction report is not reached from here.

waves.name: Build, compile and GDG definition jobs
waves.rationale: Compile procs, build jobs and generation-data-group definitions. They are listed as data jobs because a utility step reads a dataset another entry point uses, and the mode comes from DISP alone. In a refactor the compile procs have no successor, because the target has its own build. DEFGDGD defines the backup generation groups that the posting and report wave writes, so it must be replaced before wave 6.
waves.unblocks: Wave 6. DEFGDGD is the equivalent of the backup generation datasets that TRANREPT and the posting cycle write. The compile procs unblock nothing.

waves.name: Card, cross-reference and customer master refresh, statements and export
waves.rationale: The reference-data refresh jobs (card, cross-reference, customer, discount group, transaction type and category) plus the CICS close and open jobs that bracket every batch window. They rebuild a VSAM file with IDCAMS DELETE, DEFINE and REPRO from a flat file, and the work in the program is small. The wave is 26 units, but one sentence describes it: the reference masters and the window around them. CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL appear in all three Control-M folders, so they are shared plumbing. The account master refresh (ACCTFILE) is not here. The seed placed it in wave 6 because the posting program CBTRN02C also writes the account file, so the two share a wave (see wave 6).
waves.unblocks: Wave 6 needs the card, cross-reference and customer masters in the target before posting can validate a card (CBTRN02C reads the cross-reference file first), and needs the close and open jobs to open and close the online window. Also the Control-M and wrapper ordering for later waves.

waves.name: Daily posting cycle, account master refresh and transaction report
waves.rationale: All three must-not-break items are in this wave, which is the reason to hold it together. Daily posting is job POSTTRAN running CBTRN02C. The account master refresh is job ACCTFILE, which deletes, defines and reloads the account file. The transaction report is job TRANREPT running CBTRN03C, and CORPT00C submits the same procedure from an online screen. All of them write ACCTDATA, TRANSACT or TCATBALF, and run_posting.sh runs ACCTFILE, TCATBALF, TRANBKP, POSTTRAN and TRANIDX in that order, so the account reload sits in front of the posting job in the wrapper. The seed bound them as one coupled group because they write the same datasets. The wave is 29 units, over the 25 guideline. It should ship in three increments behind the scheduler and one flag, cut at the articulation points CBTRN02C and CBTRN03C: (a) ACCTFILE, TCATBALF, TRANBKP and POSTTRAN with the wrapper run_posting.sh, (b) TRANREPT, CBTRN03C, REPROC and CORPT00C, (c) interest calculation and COMBTRAN. Each increment has its own boundary and rollback. The wave plan records no deviation because the seed placement stays.
waves.unblocks: Everything that reads the account, transaction and category-balance masters: the online writers in wave 7 (COBIL00C, COTRN02C, COACTUPC read the same files) and the statement and export jobs. It is the first wave a business owner will name: the posting run, the account refresh and the report.

waves.name: Online account, card, bill payment, transaction add and user maintenance
waves.rationale: Online transactions that update the account, card, transaction and user-security masters. COACTUPC is 3,368 lines and COCRDUPC and COCRDLIC are over a thousand each. All nine make computed calls. They share the same VSAM files that wave 6 writes in batch, so they follow it, and the layout contracts are already proved by then.
waves.unblocks: The decommissioning of the VSAM masters and CICS. This is the last wave that writes to them.

waves.name: Authorization (IMS, DB2, MQ) feed and unload jobs
waves.rationale: Optional-module programs that touch IMS, DB2 or MQ. A different team, skill set and data store than the VSAM core. Four IMS and DB2 definition types are not read by the extractor (DBD, PSB, DDL, DCLGEN), so the data structures of this wave are unseen. The wave ships last and separately because none of the three must-not-break items passes through it.
waves.unblocks: Nothing in the must-not-break flows. It unblocks wave 9 by moving the authorization database to the target.

waves.name: Authorization screens and transaction type maintenance
waves.rationale: Online screens and one batch job over DB2 and IMS. COPAUS0C and COPAUS1C are a call cycle, and COPAUS0C is a god module with a self call, so it is strangled behind a facade and never ported wholesale. COTRTLIC and COTRTUPC make computed calls. The DB2 transaction-type table is an articulation point.
waves.unblocks: Retirement of the IMS and DB2 optional modules. It unblocks nothing else, so it is the right place to stop if budget ends.

unassigned.reason: Not reached by any static edge, and 28 reachable computed calls could target it, for example at app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:956. Its DDs are not mapped by any JCL in the tree (app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl:29). Ask whether it runs. If it does, it belongs with wave 6, because it reads the daily transaction, cross-reference, account and card files.
